_notice.title: Changes feed for official legal sources
_notice.what_this_is: Titles, identifiers, dates and links for legislation an official publisher has newly published or newly consolidated. It holds no text of any document. It is information, not legal advice, and it is not a complete or official list: follow the link and rely on the publisher.
_notice.credits: Titles, identifiers and dates are each publisher's. Show the attribution_line given under sources for every source whose items you show. No publisher endorses this feed.

EU/ConsolidatedLegislation.name: EU — Consolidated Legislation (In-force Texts)
EU/ConsolidatedLegislation.attribution_line: EU legislation from EUR-Lex (eur-lex.europa.eu). © European Union, 1998–2026. Consolidated texts are reused under CC BY 4.0. Extract only. Only the Official Journal of the European Union is authentic.

licence.name: EUR-Lex legal notice; consolidated texts under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International

status_lines: Only European Union documents published in the Official Journal of the European Union are deemed authentic.
Extract only, where a single article or a capped passage is shown.
conditions: Documents with special conditions are title and link only: CELEX 32023R1803 and 32008R1126 (international accounting standards), every consolidated version of them, and any regulation whose title says it adopts or amends international accounting standards.
Third-party works inside a document, and content showing identifiable private individuals, may need their own permission.

IE/Acts.name: Irish Statute Database
IE/Acts.attribution_line: Irish legislation from the electronic Irish Statute Book (irishstatutebook.ie), produced by the Office of the Attorney General. © Houses of the Oireachtas. Reused under the Oireachtas (Public Sector Information – Open Data) Licence, which incorporates CC BY 4.0. Extract only. Publication does not mean a provision is in force; see the Irish Statute Book disclaimer.

licence.name: Oireachtas (Public Sector Information – Open Data) Licence, incorporating Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International

status_lines: As enacted or as made, not revised.
Publication of legislation on the Irish Statute Book does not indicate that a provision was, or is currently, in force.
Extract only, where a single section or a capped passage is shown.

UK/LegislationGovUK.name: UK Legislation
UK/LegislationGovUK.attribution_line: UK legislation from legislation.gov.uk, published by The National Archives. © Crown and database right. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Extract only. Revised text may have changes still to be applied; see the changes noted on legislation.gov.uk.
status_lines: Revised legislation may have changes that have not yet been applied. legislation.gov.uk aims to apply an amendment within three months of its coming into force, and says with each item whether changes are outstanding.
An original version (as enacted or as made) has had no changes applied to it.
Extract only, where a single section or a capped passage is shown.
conditions: Legislation originating from the EU is derived from EUR-Lex and has a second set of terms. Acknowledge both sources and claim no official endorsement. The site suggests: "Crown © and database right material re-used under the Open Government Licence. Material derived from the European Institutions © European Union, 1998-2019 and re-used under the terms of the Commission Decision 2011/833/EU."

Statutory instruments, rules and orders made before 1987 that Westlaw UK contributed carry the attribution "Westlaw UK derived from Crown Copyright material and contributed to legislation.gov.uk". They are in their original form only.
Statutes of the Realm (1235 to 1713) contributed by British History Online carry the attribution "British History Online derived from Crown Copyright material and contributed to legislation.gov.uk".

Automated access follows the site's fair use policy. Send a user agent with a clear identifier (anonymous ones are refused, and contact details are strongly recommended), follow robots.txt, and stay under 1,500 requests in any 5 minutes. For new legislation, use the publisher's feeds and not a crawl.
